predecessors.note: Xue Ju seized Hao Yuan and rebelled at Jincheng (Lanzhou) in summer 617 (Xue Ju page; infobox reign from 13 May 617).

land.text: 'much of the territory in modern eastern Gansu' (the page), as radii round Lanzhou and Tianshui

successors.note: Xue Ju died on 3 September 618 (infobox); his son Xue Rengao was defeated by Li Shimin 'three months later' and 'annex[ed]' (Transition page); the infobox ends the Qinxing era on 30 November 618.

capitals.name: Tianshui
capitals.note: 'Xue Ju moved his capital to Tianshui after Xue Rengao captured it in fall 617.'

rulers.name: Xue Ju
rulers.note: Hegemonic Prince of Western Qin in summer 617, Emperor of Qin in fall 617; died 3 September 618.

rulers.name: Xue Rengao
rulers.note: Succeeded his father; defeated by Li Shimin in late 618.

correction.text: 'much of the territory in modern eastern Gansu' (the page), as radii round Lanzhou and Tianshui

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 617-618 for a state Cliopatria lacks: 'much of the territory in modern eastern Gansu had surrendered to Xue Ju' (infobox 'Eastern Gansu'); the Transition page adds western Shaanxi. No area on the page.

region.text: 'much of the territory in modern eastern Gansu' (the page), as radii round Lanzhou and Tianshui

ledger.note: 617: Xue Ju rebels at Jincheng. 'In summer 617' he seized Hao Yuan and declared against the Sui, first as Hegemonic Prince of Western Qin and in fall 617 as Emperor of Qin (infobox reign from 13 May 617; the page notes the sources conflict).

617: the capital moves from Jincheng to Tianshui after Xue Rengao captures it; the page places this after Xue Ju's fall 617 claim to the imperial title and gives no month (month 10 is a reading). [Reviewer ea-03-f, 2026-10-19: moved after the found event (617/5), which it preceded]

region.text: the plain west of Chang'an, Fufeng to Qianshui

ledger.note: 618: Qin and Tang fight for the Wei valley. Around the new year Li Shimin 'dealt Xue Rengao a major defeat near Fufeng'; in summer 618 Xue Ju's forces ambushed Tang commanders on the Qianshui Plain (Xianyang) and Li Shimin withdrew to Chang'an.

618: the fighting ends with the Qin's collapse. Xue Ju fell ill and died (3 September 618) and Xue Rengao was defeated 'three months later'. [Reviewer ea-03-f, 2026-10-19: month 11 changed to 12: the page has Xue Ju die on 3 September 618 and Xue Rengao defeated 'three months later']

region.text: 'much of the territory in modern eastern Gansu' (the page), as radii round Lanzhou and Tianshui

ledger.note: 618: the Qin is annexed by the Tang. 'After Xue Ju died in early 618' (Transition page, which dates his death earlier than the infobox), Xue Rengao was defeated and killed by Li Shimin, 'annexing his Qin state into Tang' (infobox: Qinxing era ends 30 November 618). [Reviewer ea-03-f, 2026-10-19: month 11 changed to 12: the page has Xue Ju die on 3 September 618 and Xue Rengao defeated 'three months later']

wars.name: Tang campaign against Xue Ju and Xue Rengao

zones.text: the Wei valley west of Chang'an

wars.outcome: Tang victory: Xue Ju died in 618 and Xue Rengao's defeat ended the Qin.

certainty.note: A rebel region of eastern Gansu; the page gives regions, no boundary.

sources.title: Xue Ju
sources.note: Summer 617 rising, Jincheng and Tianshui, eastern Gansu, Fufeng and Qianshui 618, death 3 September 618, Xue Rengao.

sources.title: Transition from Sui to Tang
sources.note: The Qin in the list of rival regimes (eastern Gansu and western Shaanxi, 'by 617' to 618).

notes: REBEL STATE. The two pages disagree on the date of Xue Ju's death ('early 618' on the Transition page, 3 September 618 on the Xue Ju infobox) and the sources on the start date of his reign; the dossier follows the Xue Ju page. The region is a pair of radii read from 'eastern Gansu'. Cliopatria has no row for the Qin of Xue Ju (the row 'Western Qin' is the Sixteen Kingdoms' state, slug western-qin).
